what_it_does: Analog-to-digital converters (chips that turn real-world analog signals into digital numbers) face a trade-off between speed and precision. Incremental converters combine two approaches: a fast, power-efficient successive-approximation design with a more precise noise-shaping algorithm, but at very high precision they become slow. The challenge is reducing thermal noise—random noise from the physics of capacitor circuits—without using expensive amplifiers that consume power the whole time. This paper introduces a clever power-saving technique: the amplifier only turns on during the brief noise-cancellation phase, not throughout the entire conversion. This drastically cuts power consumption while maintaining high precision and conversion rates suitable for sensor applications.
